conviction_note: Q3 itself is pre-framed as the trough and consensus ($2.49 / ~$672.5M) sits inside the company guide, so the print turns on whether the reaffirmed FY revenue guide (implying a record ~$800M Q4) is held; Fortinet's Oct 28 print (+37% product revenue, raised FY) argues the firewall market is strong enough for the slipped appliance deals to close, against a name whose last two guides were sold (-19.6%, -8.2%) and a +13.9% 20-day run-up that has already given back 6.7% this week; the evidence nets near zero (impact_sum -0.6), so p_up 49 on a 9-point move, and the two measurements agree that there is no strong lean.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus non-GAAP EPS $2.49 and revenue ~$672.5M (finviz/ preview 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407868/check-points-rally-meets-its-trough-quarter-as-q4-rebound-story-faces-proof ; EPS $2.49 also MarketBeat). Company Q3 guide from the 2026-07-30 call: revenue $665-685M (some sources print $655M low end), subscription $332-343M, non-GAAP EPS $2.43-2.53 (https://www.webull.com/news/15364638754350080). FY2026 guide reaffirmed: non-GAAP EPS $10.05-10.85, revenue ~$2.77-2.85B (sources differ, MarketBeat $2.8-2.9B), implying ~6.5% Q4 growth / ~$800M record Q4. The calendar's $1.99 matches neither non-GAAP (~$2.48) nor GAAP (~$0.70 below non-GAAP, ~$1.78) and is disowned. Pre-Q2 estimates ($2.58 / ~$696-699M) are stale. Bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing EPS sources.
positioning_check: Short interest 5.8M shares, 4.9 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement (down from 6.2M / 5.5 days on 09-15) per https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/chkp/short-interest/ ; MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CHKP/, read 2026-10-30) shows 7.54% of float, 6.87 days, down 4.97% m/m. Moderate, falling, not crowded. Borrow fee ~0.3%. Baseline skew -3.39 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.53, event-implied move 9.08% (straddle 11.59% to 2026-11-20). Tape: 20d +13.85%, 5d -6.68%, -27% from 52w high; stock ~$148.4-148.9 intraday 10-30, down ~3% on the day after $153.50 on 10-29; preview says it rallied ~29% off post-Q2 lows to ~$159 by 10-26. Analyst stance Hold (9 Buy / 18 Hold, avg PT $150.39).

findings.finding: Fortinet reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-28 (after CHKP last spoke on 07-30): product revenue $765.0M, +37% y/y, billings $2.34B +29%, total revenue +20%, FY2026 revenue guide raised to $8.125-8.215B; its 10-Q attributes product growth to secure-networking hardware incl. higher-performance appliances and AI-infrastructure deployments. CHKP's own Q2 product revenue fell 14% and it guided a similar decline in Q3, with large appliance deals pushed into Q4 which its FY guide (record ~$800M Q4) depends on. A firewall market this strong makes the Q4 slip-and-close story more plausible (supportive of the guide being held), though it also shows CHKP's decline is company-specific (share/go-to-market), not market-wide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHKP trades on the forward revenue guide: 2026-04-30 FY revenue outlook lowered, -19.6% (bmo, volume-confirmed); 2026-07-30 EPS beat but Q3 revenue guide below consensus, -8.2%; 2025-10-28 billings +20% and beat, about +7% intraday (fool.com).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market read Fortinet as positive read-through for CHKP's Q4 appliance pipeline, CHKP would have risen on 10-29/10-30; instead it fell ~1.1% on 10-29 and ~3% on 10-30, so the price is treating the FTNT print either as share loss or not at all. No CHKP-specific note tying FTNT's hardware strength to CHKP's slipped deals was found.
findings.independence: Sector-wide rally on 'improving enterprise security spending' lifted CHKP +3.8% on 2026-10-23 (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Check+Point+Software+rises+as+cybersecurity+shares+gain+on+stronger+spending+outlook). FTNT 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001262039/000126203926000027/ftnt-20260930.htm) is the same company's document, so it counts once.

findings.finding: Management's own FY2026 guide (reaffirmed 07-30, unchanged since the May cut) is back-end loaded: CFO Golan said Q4 needs ~6.5% growth to reach the midpoint (analyst Tindle: ~$800M, a record quarter), after more large appliance deals slipped from Q3 into Q4 than May assumed; CEO: 'a lot riding on Q4'. Any narrowing of the FY range toward the low end on Nov 2 is the line this stock has sold twice this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-30 FY outlook cut: -19.6%; 2026-07-30 soft Q3 revenue guide with FY held: -8.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 2026-10-26 preview names exactly this risk, and the stock ran +29% off its lows into it, which looks like the market leaning on the 'Q3 trough, Q4 rebound' framing rather than discounting a trim; a fully priced guide-trim risk would show put skew, and skew is call-bid (-3.39).
findings.independence: https://finviz.com/news/407868/check-points-rally-meets-its-trough-quarter-as-q4-rebound-story-faces-proof (2026-10-26) independently flags 'any narrowing toward the low end'. Shares the transcript with finding on memory costs only for context.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-26 CHKP launched Firewall-as-a-Subscription (3-year commitment, monthly/annual payments, no upfront hardware, available through partners from 2026-11-01), which converts part of the appliance purchase that Q4's record product quarter depends on into ratable revenue; management may cite the model shift on Nov 2 to reframe or trim Q4 product revenue, or present it as a subscription tailwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior model-transition disclosure at CHKP; the stock has reacted to revenue guide changes (-19.6%, -8.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: The launch was covered as product news (IT trade press) and the 10-26 earnings preview does not connect it to the Q4 revenue guide; if analysts had modelled a revenue-recognition headwind, FY revenue estimates would have moved and notes would mention it. Inference only: the company has not said what share of Q4 deals could move to the subscription.
findings.independence: Proxy/inference; TechSpot coverage (https://techspot.com/news/114368-check-point-turning-network-firewalls-cloud-based-subscriptions.html) confirms terms, same press release.

findings.finding: Memory (DRAM) cost inflation is squeezing appliance margins: CHKP's Q2 gross margin slipped to 87% on higher memory costs and the CFO said he is spending significant time securing inventory; Wedbush named CHKP among the most exposed and noted a 5% Quantum price increase; Fortinet's Q4 guide has non-GAAP gross margin at 78-80%. Small drag on Q3 margin and on customer appetite for hardware.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the line CHKP moved on; product is a minority of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced (Q2 already disclosed it, EPS guide includes it); filed small for the risk that the Q4 hardware ramp meets customer hesitation on price.
findings.independence: CHKP Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15364638754350080) and FTNT Q4 GM guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001262039/000126203926000024/ftntq3-2026ex991.htm).

findings.finding: EPS cushion: Q2 non-GAAP EPS $2.55 beat consensus $2.45, helped by a $28M R&D expense reduction under Israel's new R&D tax incentive program, a $14M hedging benefit and ~2.5M shares repurchased for $325M in Q2 (plus a $2B buyback expansion on 2026-05-11); consensus $2.49 sits at the guide midpoint, so another EPS beat is likely, on a line this stock does not pay for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-30 EPS beat of $0.10 was met with -8.2%; Feb 2026 a tax-aided EPS beat with revenue in line saw a modest gain. Beats are sold when the revenue guide disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: Whisper EPS $2.54 vs consensus $2.49 shows a beat is expected, so mostly priced; kept small.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: shares ran ~29% off post-Q2 lows to ~$159 (+13.9% over 20 sessions, sentiment 'from bearish to nearly neutral') on the trough/rebound framing and the Oct 23 sector rally, then gave back 6.7% in five sessions to ~$148 by 10-30; calls bid over puts (skew -3.39); short interest moderate and falling (4.9-6.9 days). A run-up into a back-end-loaded guide leaves room for sell-the-news, though this week's drawdown has unwound part of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 print came after a recovery and fell 8.2%; Q1 fell 19.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Call-bid skew shows the option market leaning up, not hedging a disappointment; the 5-day drop suggests some de-risking already, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d +13.85, run_up_5d -6.68, skew -3.39); MarketBeat quote 10-30 -3.0% (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CHKP/).

findings.finding: Chief Product Officer Nataly Kremer sold 3,185 shares on 2026-10-22 (~$478k reported 10-26); 7 insider sells and 0 buys over the past year. Routine size.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public and immaterial; filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: ~300 go-to-market hires by year-end, impact on sales expected in Q1-Q2 2027; 2027 margin commentary deferred, may be addressed on the call but the revenue effect is 2027.

baseline_tension: The skew is call-bid and the 20-day run-up is large, while the company's own guide makes the print a test of a back-end-loaded Q4; what I found (strong Fortinet read-through vs CHKP's own record of selling off on its guide) roughly offsets, so it neither confirms nor fights the skew strongly.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): consensus sits inside the company guide and the back-end-loaded FY guide risk is named in the wire preview, so the guide-trim finding shrank from -1.0 to -0.6.
Lesson 7 (positioning, skew call-bid, short interest moderate and falling): positioning finding trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4 and p_up moved from 48 to 49.
Pessimism artefact and 'peer print after the company last spoke' (what has worked): Fortinet finding left at +1.0, not cut.
FPI reaction history rebuilt from confirmed releases (lesson on wrong events); abs_move_pct kept at 9 on the event-implied move and a confirmed-print median near 8.
